C-PLANS-COMPACT-TOOLBAR-259.Summary: Replace the overloaded plans filter row with one designer-led, stable toolbar: persistent current/archive navigation, always-visible search, compact progressive disclosure for rare filters, and removable human-readable filter tokens.
C-PLANS-COMPACT-TOOLBAR-259.Problem: The plans screen gives the primary lifecycle mode the same hierarchy as secondary filters. Current/archive is hidden in a dropdown, rare fields occupy the full working row, the filter state is hard to read after interaction, and concurrent requests may render a stale list or detail. The result requires extra clicks, causes overflow on constrained screens and obscures the current user context.

Goals.Goal: Expose `Текущие | Архив` as a persistent one-action segmented control backed by the existing server `status` query.
Keep search permanently available while moving existing rare filters into one compact disclosure with `Фильтры N`, individual filter tokens and a rare-filter-only reset.
Adapt proven semantic patterns from Docomator and Planer Solving without copying their CSS, assets or architecture.
Preserve valid search, filter and selection context, clear invalid stale detail, and prevent an older response from replacing a newer user choice.
Provide stable desktop, constrained desktop and mobile geometry, keyboard operation, visible focus, 44 px targets and deterministic prefers-reduced-motion behavior.

Constraints.Constraint: The verified base is main commit e6c767949a19a9232e19d95fd8f0632d978f9e69 with tree c786711af18cbf8616ad624a21db4f2b147ca22d.
Issue 259 is authoritative and supersedes overlapping toolbar issues 249, 252, 254, 255 and 257. Parent issue 236 remains the larger plans UX program.
No API route, SQLite schema, migration, plan lifecycle command, archive impact calculation, document intake, source-row decision or plan-detail redesign is introduced.
The existing plans query remains the source of truth. UI controls may only form its parameters and must not create a second persisted filter or lifecycle state.
Lifecycle value, toolbar geometry, search text and filter values are never-learn in this change. Usage statistics may not reorder, preselect or hide controls.
The implementation remains dependency-free, autonomous and fully functional without Internet, Docomator, LLM or external assets.
Reference repositories are design evidence only: no source code, CSS, icons, fonts or licensed assets are copied.
The separate mobile list-to-detail navigation from issue 258 is not implemented here; the toolbar and filter disclosure must nevertheless remain usable at 390 px without horizontal spill.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Change the fields or semantics supported by the plans API.
Add saved filter presets, adaptive ranking, analytics or a new design-system dependency.
Archive or restore a plan from the lifecycle segment.
Implement reversible exclusion of recognized source rows; that remains a later vertical under parent issue 236.
Redesign meetings or their templates; issue 237 remains sequentially blocked until plans changes are terminally archived.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The visible plans toolbar contains search, a persistent `Текущие | Архив` tablist and one `Фильтры` button; the old visible lifecycle dropdown and always-expanded rare filter row are absent.
One click, tap, Enter, Space, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home or End changes lifecycle view and produces the existing server query with `status=active|archived` without modifying a plan.
Search remains unchanged across lifecycle and rare-filter changes. A selection survives only if present in the latest result; otherwise detail clears before loading and falls back deterministically.
Kind, period, direction and responsible filters open in one compact panel, apply immediately, and are reflected by a correct `Фильтры N` count.

Every active rare filter has one human-readable token with a 44 px remove action. Removing a token clears exactly that control, while `Сбросить` clears only rare filters and preserves search and lifecycle.
Escape and outside click close the disclosure, focus returns to the trigger, and reopening shows the authoritative current values.
Request sequence guards prevent an older list or detail response from overwriting a newer lifecycle, search, filter or selection action.
Empty states distinguish an empty current collection, an empty archive and a non-empty filter/search that happens to match nothing.
The layout does not overlap the sidebar or create page-level horizontal scrolling at desktop 1440×900, constrained desktop 1024×768, mobile 390×844 and 200 percent zoom.
Selection and disclosure motion is interruptible, limited to 120–220 ms and never delays data. With prefers-reduced-motion the state changes instantly or with short opacity only.
An independent kafedra-design-audit records the actual desktop, constrained, mobile, keyboard, focus, overflow, contrast and reduced-motion result with no unresolved blocker or major finding.

Focused unit and Playwright tests, npm check, docs check, complete project tests, GRACE final, release, offline and database gates succeed on one exact head before squash merge; post-merge CI succeeds before a separate archive-only applied transition.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The exact implementation head demonstrates the real plans screen, not a synthetic fixture: one-action lifecycle navigation, compact progressive filtering, readable active conditions, no stale response and stable responsive geometry.

Assumptions.Assumption: The existing `/api/plans` endpoint already accepts `status`, `q`, `kind`, `periodKey`, `direction` and `responsible` and returns authoritative items and facets.
The existing archive/restore API and impact flow remain correct and can call a public plans-view setter after a successful lifecycle operation.
Current application CSS variables and native controls are sufficient to implement the toolbar without a new runtime dependency.
